description: A paper plane brings a treasure map! Fly up for a bird's-eye view, read a map key and a compass rose, find squares on a grid, and follow a route to the treasure.

youtube.title: Treasure Map Quest! Map Skills for Kids: Key, Compass and Grid | Grade 2 | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
A paper plane lands with a map scrap: 3 east, 3 north. Robo, Cat, Dog and Pig fly up for a bird's-eye view, turn the playroom into map symbols, read the map key, learn north, east, south and west, and find squares like B4 on a grid.
Follow the route to the treasure, see why Cat's shortcut hits a tree, and solve the second clue.
Try at home: draw a map of your bedroom from above and hide a toy.

do.text: Treasure Map Quest
A paper plane! It flew in through the window.
There's something written on it.
A tree, a blue oval, and a big X. And the words...
3 east, 3 north.
Sniff, sniff. Treasure?
Only if we can read the map.
A map shows a place as if you're a bird, high above.
Let's fly up and see our playroom like a bird does!
bird's-eye view
Wow! From up here, things look flat. We only see their tops.
And I can see the whole playroom at once.
A map shows where things are,
and how to get from place to place.
On a map, we draw each thing as a simple symbol.
symbol
The house becomes a red square.
The tree becomes a green triangle.
The bush is a green circle. The pond is a blue oval.
And the flower is a pink star.
But why draw symbols? Why not little pictures?
Symbols are quick to draw and easy to read.
Fun fact: some of the oldest maps were carved in clay,
long, long ago.
And astronauts used maps of the Moon to plan where to land!
But how do we know what each symbol means? We need a key!
map key
Oink! I'm the keeper of the map key.
A red square means house.
A green triangle means tree.
A green circle means bush.
What does the blue oval mean?
A pond!
A pink star means flower.
And a red X marks the treasure!
What does the green triangle mean? Look at the key!
A tree! Point to the tree on the map.
A map key is sometimes called a legend.
legend
So the key is like a dictionary for the map.
House, tree, bush, pond, flower, treasure. All in my key!
Exactly! Without a key, a map is just shapes.
Now, which way is east? We need a compass rose.
North!
East!
South!
West!
On most maps, north is at the top. East is to the right.
They go round clockwise: north, east, south, west.
So when north is up, west is on the left.
But why is north at the top?
Map makers agreed to put it there, so every map matches.
Fun fact: a compass needle points north.
That's because the Earth acts like a giant magnet!
Let me try. I face north, and turn east!
Robo, that's west!
East is on your right when you face north.
Oops! Right hand. East!
Stand up and face the screen.
That's north. Point to the right. East!
Point behind you. South! Point to the left. West!
Our map has a grid, like a game board.
grid
Letters go across: A, B, C, D, E.
Numbers go up: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
To find a square, read the letter first, then the number.
Which square is the tree in?
B4! Column B, row 4.
B4
Now find the pond.
E2! Column E, row 2.
E2
And the X? Where is the treasure?
D4! The treasure is in square D4.
D4
Which square has the flower?
D5! Right above the treasure.
D5
And the house, where we start?
A1! The corner square.
A1
Letter first, then number. Like an address for a square.
Turn with me! A quarter turn on every line.
North to the top,
east to the right,
south to the bottom,
west takes flight!
Here's our own memory sentence: Now Every Snail Waves!
North, East, South, West. Waving snails. I like it.
North to the top, east to the right,
south to the bottom, west takes flight!
Dog, start at the house, square A1.
The map says 3 east. Count the steps out loud with Dog!
1, 2, 3 east. Now Dog is at D1. Then 3 north!
1, 2, 3 north. Dog is at D4!
Treasure! A present!
3 east, then 3 north. The route worked!
I had a shortcut. Watch: 3 north first, then east.
Oops. The tree at B4 is in the way!
A route is a plan. Go around: up to A5, then east.
Maps help you choose a route that works. Lesson learned.
And counting squares keeps you from getting lost.
Challenge! Pig found a second clue.
The second treasure is 2 squares west of the pond.
Hidden under a bush!
West means toward the left of the map, away from the pond.
Start at the pond, E2. Go 2 west. Which square?
E2, D2, C2! The bush!
Check the key. A green circle means bush. Yes!
Dog, go dig!
A ball! Best treasure ever!
The map-key keeper says: well done, explorers!
Your turn to read a clue. Start at A1, go 4 east, 1 north.
A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, then up to E2. The pond!
Make up your own clues at home.
It's fun to be the map maker.
Quiz time! What does a map key tell you?
What the symbols mean!
On most maps, which way is at the top?
North!
Start at A1. Go 2 squares east. Where are you?
Why didn't Cat's shortcut work?
The tree at B4 was in the way!
Four for four! You're map experts.
Look what we found!
Navigator approved.
Draw a map of your bedroom,
from above, with a key and a compass.
Hide toys only in safe, open places. No climbing! Bye!
